A prior session just shipped a new feature on `/admin/nodes`: each node card/row now has an editable "Lease cost" dollar input and computed "MRR"/"Margin" figures, added in commit `71efb79c48` (files: `prisma/schema.prisma` — new `Node.monthlyCostCents`, `lib/actions-nodes.ts` — new `setNodeMonthlyCost` action, `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx` — new `NodeCostInput` component, `app/admin/nodes/page.tsx`). This was verified at the DB/persistence/build level already, but NOBODY has actually looked at it in a real browser yet — that's your job.

Task: log into the Nxeon admin panel as an admin (check this repo's own test/e2e conventions for how admin auth is normally done in an automated context — e.g. `scripts/e2e-test.ts` if it exists, or a documented admin test account/session-minting approach in CLAUDE.md), navigate to `/admin/nodes` on production (or staging if production admin access isn't safely scriptable — check which is appropriate), and take a real screenshot. Specifically verify:

1. The new "Lease cost" input renders correctly for each node, with a clear "not set" placeholder for nodes with no cost entered yet (all 4 real nodes — primary, node-2, node-3, node-4 — currently have `monthlyCostCents: null`, so you should see the "not set" state on all of them).
2. The computed "MRR" figure renders correctly and looks sane (real numbers reported by the prior work: primary ~$85.30, node-2 ~$102.00, node-3 ~$109.42, node-4 ~$36.99).
3. Try actually entering a real cost value into one node's input (e.g. type "50" for a $50/mo lease cost) and confirm: it saves (the input commits on blur — click away or tab out), the page reflects the new value on reload, and the "Margin" figure (MRR minus cost) now appears/computes correctly for that node.
4. Check the visual layout doesn't look broken — no overlapping text, no layout shift issues, fits reasonably within the existing RAM/CPU/DISK/BACKUP stat-block style already on that page (matching screenshots the owner shared earlier this session showing that page's existing design).
5. After testing, reset the value you entered back to null/not-set (blank the input, commit) so you don't leave test data in a real customer-facing admin page — this is a real production database.

This is a READ+one-test-write-then-revert task on a real admin page — be careful to actually revert your test edit at the end. Do not touch anything else on the page or in the app beyond this one node's cost field.

Report back: whether the layout renders correctly (attach description of what you saw, or a screenshot if your environment supports capturing one), confirmation the save/reload/margin-calculation flow works as described, and confirmation you reverted your test edit.
